hazard: Lack of understanding of police response to AWOL patient
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Nimo Younis
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: C&l ward staff did not have a proper understanding of what action the MPS would take in what circumstances, following the report of a patient absent without leave.
concerns.hazard: lack of understanding of police response to AWOL patient

concerns.quote: C&l ward staff did not have a proper understanding of what action the MPS required others to take in order to prompt the police to progress the matter further.
concerns.hazard: lack of understanding of required actions to prompt police progression

concerns.quote: C&l ward staff did not have a practical plan as to how to take that action with the resources at their disposal.
concerns.hazard: lack of practical plan to act

concerns.quote: C&l ward staff did not have a proper understanding of what key information they needed to provide the MPS in order to trigger a police missing person enquiry, or to escalate an existing enquiry.
concerns.hazard: lack of understanding of required information for police enquiry

concerns.quote: C&l ward staff did not promptly or fully utilise the significant potential of their patient's friends, who were ultimately the route by which Nimo Younis was found, and who would certainly have acted sooner if they had appreciated the lack of action being taken - whatever the reason for that lack of action.
concerns.hazard: failure to utilise patient's friends for locating

concerns.quote: The MPS decision makers, particularly the night time duty inspector, did not have all the information that the MPS held when they were making decisions.
concerns.hazard: lack of information for MPS decision makers

reports.title: Heather Findlay: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: Response The MPS currently has the Affinity Protocol in place and has done since September 2021.This is a collaborative partnership between local policing, NHS Trusts and mental health service providers, the aim of which is to achieve mutual understanding of each partner's responsibilities in respect of those patients detained under the Mental Health Act and who may abscond.
promises.summary: MPS has the Affinity Protocol in place since September 2021 to clarify responsibilities for patients detained under Mental Health Act who may abscond.

concerns.quote: When Ms Findlay ran off, the HCA escorting her was so panicked that she did not even think of following
no ELFT policy for what those instructions should be or even what they could include
concerns.hazard: absence of guidance for staff following absconded patients

concerns.quote: clinician calling the police in what the clinician perceived to be an emergency situation might not be assisted by the police
concerns.hazard: police may not respond to mental health emergencies

concerns.quote: the police would not necessarily attend, even if called direct by a hospital staff member in the street following a patient about whom they are worried
concerns.hazard: police non-response to patient absconding calls

concerns.quote: Right Care Right Person (RCRP) is an operational model developed by Humberside Police that changes the way the emergency services respond to calls involving concerns about mental health
concerns.hazard: inconsistent mental health emergency protocols across police forces

concerns.quote: the grab pack prepared by ELFT for the MPS in such a situation was printed out and handed to police if & when the police attended the ward
concerns.hazard: inconsistent risk grading and information sharing between trust and police

links.explanation: Both reports highlight uncertainty about how the Metropolitan Police Service will respond when hospital staff report a patient who has absconded or is causing concern.
